subject: Performance SLO & Autoscaling follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wallace <sam.wallace@acme.ai>, Jenna Park <jenna@acme.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-01T15:12:00Z
Subject: Performance SLO & Autoscaling follow-up

Hi Sam / Jenna,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and the items we said we'd follow up on so we have alignment for the mutual action plan: I attached a spreadsheet (SLO_requirements.xlsx) and the draft Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf.

Call recap (short):
- Target SLOs: p95 end-to-end latency <= 400ms for non-streaming requests. For streaming interactions we discussed start-of-stream <= 200ms and per-chunk latency <100ms.
- Throughput / concurrency: sustained baseline ~200 qps, expected peak bursts up to ~1,000 qps for short windows (1-5 minutes).
- Streaming ratio: ~30% of calls are streaming (chat UX), the rest are non-streaming generative calls.
- Autoscaling / burst asks: you asked about scale-up times, warm pools, and queueing behavior — see questions below.

Questions we still need from you (to finalize config and pricing):
1) Confirm traffic shape: do you expect multiple daily bursts or occasional large events? If you can share a 7-day traffic CSV that shows qps over time that would be ideal.
2) For streaming calls: is soft start (accept token-by-token streaming) acceptable or do you need guaranteed per-chunk latency under 100ms for every token?
3) Any hard blackout windows or regulatory constraints for spinning up additional capacity?

What Redwood will provide (summary):
- Recommendation for warm pool sizing + min nodes to meet your SLOs.
- Autoscaler configuration: target scaling step sizes and policies, queueing behavior, and documented fallbacks (smaller model variant or degraded rate-limited path) if scaling can't keep up.
- A draft SLA appendix we can attach to the deal once we lock in numbers.

Next steps: please review the attached SLO spreadsheet, and if you can share the traffic CSV and preferred go-live window we will propose a concrete warm-pool + autoscaling config and estimate for Dedicated capacity (or hosted burst pricing) by Friday.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLO_requirements.xlsx (xlsx)]
[Attachment: Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf (pdf)]

From: Sam Wallace <sam.wallace@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Park <jenna@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-03-02T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Autoscaling follow-up

Marissa — thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: we do expect predictable daily spikes tied to marketing sends (roughly 9am and 3pm PST) plus an occasional large release-day spike that could last 10-20 minutes.

Answers to your questions:
1) We'll export and share a 7-day qps CSV tomorrow (tops).
2) For streaming: user-facing chat UI requires smooth streaming; we care about perceived latency. If start-of-stream is within 200ms and subsequent chunk delivery keeps pace so the UI doesn't stutter, that's acceptable. Per-chunk 100ms is a good target but we can tolerate occasional blips.
3) No regulatory blackout windows. We do have a compliance review for audit logs, but that shouldn't block capacity.

Two practical questions for you / Dev:
A) What are realistic warm-pool targets to hit p95 400ms for non-streaming at our baseline (200 qps) and peak (1,000 qps)?
B) How does Redwood handle queueing when all warm nodes are saturated — is there a soft-queue with backpressure and retry semantics or do requests fail fast? We prefer graceful degradation rather than hard errors.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Wallace
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme AI

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wallace <sam.wallace@acme.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-03T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Autoscaling follow-up

Sam / Marissa — quick technical note from the infra side to give concrete numbers and address the queueing question. High level answers below; happy to jump on a brief tech call.

Warm pools and scale behavior (Redwood Dedicated / Hosted burst):
- Warm pools: recommended to reserve per-customer warm instances (not shared) for predictable SLOs. For your profile (200 qps baseline, 1,000 qps bursts) we typically recommend a min warm pool of 2 GPU nodes sized for your model + an autoscaling burst policy.
- Scale steps: our autoscaler increments capacity in 1-GPU steps per scale action, with a configurable cool-down. Default safe config: add 1 GPU every 30s under sustained queue/backlog.
- Cold start: full cold-start (spin up from zero) to ready typically 6-8 minutes depending on provider image pull times; warm pool nodes are kept ready to avoid that.
- Burst capacity: we support short-term burst multipliers (3-5x) where we can hand off to a warm-burst pool; for you, plan for 3x baseline (so warm pool + burst buffer covers ~600 qps) and request additional dedicated burst capacity for larger events.

Queueing and graceful degradation:
- Soft queue: when all warm nodes are busy we provide a small request queue (configurable) with backpressure and retry semantics. Default queue window is 15s before attempting fallback.
- Fallbacks: if queue timeout triggers we can route to a smaller, lower-cost model variant (reduced quality) or return a rate-limited response indicating retry-after. We favor graceful degradation over outright failures for critical UX.

Recommendation for Acme (initial):
- Min warm nodes: 2 (handles baseline user concurrency with headroom).
- Burst strategy: warm-burst pool sized to 3x baseline (~600 qps). Configure autoscaler to add 1 GPU every 30s with a max burst up to 5x for provider-backed instances (policy-based).
- Streaming: ensure at least one warm node is dedicated to streaming traffic (reduces tokenization/generation overhead); use continuous batching and a KV cache.

I'll prepare a small design note and a proposed autoscaling YAML snippet if you want — can attach to the mutual action plan.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Action items for Acme:

2) Confirm go-live window (target) so we can size warm pools for the ramp.
3) If you have an internal threshold for acceptable degraded-model quality (e.g., reduce model size from X to Y), let us know so we can encode that in the fallback policy.

Proposed follow-up: 30-minute tech sync on Thursday at 11am PT to review the autoscaling snippet and confirm fallback behavior. I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm availability.
